cards.text: Then the prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him on the first day of the eleventh month of the twelfth year. God calls him "Son of man" and gives him a message about the city of Tyre. Tyre has been running its mouth about Jerusalem, and God heard every word.

cards.question: Jerusalem lies in ruins. How does the city of Tyre react?

answers.text: It gloats and expects to gain
It panics and shuts its gates

cards.text: Tyre says, "Aha! The gate to the nations is broken; it has swung open to me; now that she lies in ruins I will be filled". That's the coworker who hears you got let go and asks, "So who gets your parking spot?"

cards.question: True or false: After Tyre's "Aha!" over Jerusalem, God says He is on Tyre's side.

cards.text: God says, "Behold, O Tyre, I am against you". He'll raise up many nations against Tyre, as the sea brings up its waves.

cards.question: The nations that roll in against Tyre like waves will ___ her walls and towers.

cards.text: And God isn't stopping at the walls. He says, "I will scrape the soil from her and make her a bare rock."

cards.question: Once Tyre is a bare rock in the sea, God says it will become a place to spread ___.

cards.text: Tyre becomes plunder for the nations, and her villages on the mainland fall by the sword. Then God names the king He's bringing against Tyre from the north.

cards.question: Which king is God bringing against Tyre from the north?

cards.text: God calls Nebuchadnezzar king of kings, and he's bringing horses, chariots, cavalry and a great company of troops. That's not an army, friend, that's RUSH HOUR with swords.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar builds a ramp to Tyre's walls and raises his shields. What does he aim at those walls?

cards.text: Battering rams on the walls, axes on the towers, and his horses kick up so much dust it covers the city.

cards.question: True or false: When Nebuchadnezzar rides through Tyre's gates, the walls shake from the noise.

cards.text: Cavalry, wagons and chariots, all rattling those walls. I know that rattle, friend, because every time somebody yanked my junk drawer open I shook just like that, and they were only looking for tape.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar's horses trample every street, and Tyre's mighty pillars fall. What happens to Tyre's wealth and merchandise?

cards.text: Then they tear down Tyre's beautiful homes and throw the stones, timber and soil into the water. Not in a pile, friend, in the WATER.

cards.question: As Tyre falls apart, God says He will silence the sound of Tyre's ___.
True or false: God says Tyre will be rebuilt someday.

cards.text: God says Tyre will never be rebuilt, "for I, the LORD, have spoken". When He says it, friend, there's no second draft.
Then God speaks to Tyre about how the coastlands will take the news. "Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your downfall, when the wounded groan at the slaughter in your midst?"

cards.question: Tyre falls and the coastlands quake. What do the princes of the sea do?

cards.text: They take off their robes, strip off their embroidered garments and sit right on the ground. When the princes of the sea are sitting on the floor, you KNOW the meeting did not go well.

cards.question: True or false: The princes of the sea stay calm about Tyre's fall.

cards.text: They're clothed with terror, trembling every moment, appalled over Tyre. Then they lament for her.

cards.question: The princes of the sea lament over Tyre. What do they remember Tyre for?

cards.text: They say, "How you have perished, O city of renown inhabited by seafaring men". She was powerful on the sea, along with her people.

cards.question: The princes say Tyre and her people once imposed ___ on all peoples.

cards.text: The city that imposed terror now leaves the coastlands trembling on the day of her downfall. And God says He'll make Tyre a desolate city like other deserted cities.

cards.question: Tyre is about to be desolate. What does God say He will raise up against her?

cards.text: The mighty waters cover Tyre. Then God says He'll bring her down with those who descend to the Pit, to dwell in the earth below like the ancient ruins.

cards.question: True or false: God says Tyre will still be set in splendor in the land of the living.
God says Tyre will be ___ but will never be ___.

cards.text: God says He'll make Tyre an object of horror, and she will be no more. And that's how the message ends: "declares the Lord GOD."

findings.problem: The setup says Tyre "has been running its mouth about Jerusalem." This tells the baker Tyre is talking against Jerusalem, which rules out "It mourns and sends help" and "It panics and shuts its gates" on card 2 before the baker chooses.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card holds three beats: Tyre becomes plunder, the mainland villages fall by the sword, and God is about to name the king coming from the north.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Verse 6 ends with "Then they will know that I am the LORD," the stated purpose of the judgment. No card tells it. Verse 11's "He will slaughter your people with the sword" is also never told, on card 16 or anywhere else.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "That's RUSH HOUR with swords" mixes the everyday image (rush hour traffic) with the Bible setting (swords).

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 9 already told the baker that "Tyre becomes plunder for the nations" (v5). That gives away the right answer here, "It gets plundered" (v12), which repeats the same idea.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "When the princes of the sea are sitting on the floor, you KNOW the meeting did not go well" puts the princes from the passage into the everyday meeting image, so the comparison and the Bible setting are blended.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The two blanks (sought / found) test the exact wording of verse 21, which the baker hasn't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason out this pair over choices like "visited" or "praised."

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: After card 3, the story cards (5, 7, 9, 11, 14) are plain paraphrase with no reactions, comparisons or humor. The stop reads as a flat summary, not as Papa Dorin telling it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Several story cards retell God's future pronouncements in the present tense as if they were narrated events, without "God says": stop 1 card 9 ("Tyre becomes plunder... her villages... fall by the sword"), stop 1 card 17 ("Then they tear down Tyre's beautiful homes") and stop 2 card 11 ("The mighty waters cover Tyre"). In verses 3-21 these are all things God says He will do.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, may Papa Dorin retell God's predictions in the present tense as story events, or must each card mark them as what God says will happen?
